curequantile

The curequantile package can be used to fit quantile regression model for censored time-to-event data with a cure fraction.

Installation

You can install the development version of curequantile by issuing:

remotes::install_github("kelliejarcher/curequantile")

Example

After loading the relevant R packages,

library(curequantile)
library(survival)
library(maxLik)
#> Loading required package: miscTools
#> 
#> Please cite the 'maxLik' package as:
#> Henningsen, Arne and Toomet, Ott (2011). maxLik: A package for maximum likelihood estimation in R. Computational Statistics 26(3), 443-458. DOI 10.1007/s00180-010-0217-1.
#> 
#> If you have questions, suggestions, or comments regarding the 'maxLik' package, please use its GitHub page and the issues there:
#> https://github.com/arne-henningsen/maxLik

a cure quantile regression model can be fit using the curequantile function.

data("breast_data")
fit_breast <- curequantile(Surv(log(Time), Delta) ~ Age + Size,
  data = breast_data, subset = 1:200)

The coef() function extracts the parameter estimates at a specific quantile tau.

coefficients <- coef(fit_breast, tau = 0.25)
names(coefficients)
#> [1] "gamma_est" "eta_est"   "beta_est"
coefficients$gamma_est
#> (Intercept)         Age        Size 
#> -4.41474759  0.03760906  0.03203235

Here, gamma_est contains the incidence parameter estimates, while beta_est contains the latency parameter estimates at the specified quantile, tau. Finally, eta_est gives the conditional probabilities of being susceptible, and therefore has a length equal to the number of rows in the input data frame. Alternatively, print() prints the coefficients at the user-specified quantile tau to the console.

The summary() function returns the parameter estimates, bootstrap standard error estimates, Z-test, p-value, and bootstrap confidence interval for incidence covariates and the latency covariates at the indicated quantile, tau.

The plot() function produces a plot of the quantile estimate and corresponding confidence interval for each covariate over the range of the user-specified quantiles tau.

Other functions designed to handle the resulting model object include: dim(), formula(), logLik(), nobs(), and predict().
